quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.
Can make you a better rider.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream. This happens quickly and affects the brain fast.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: You need to stay aware of everything around you. Mirrors alone are not enough. Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that is properly fastened is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handlebars.
Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you control the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injuries. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: To shift up to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push down.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, put your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is quieter than car horns. Riders should use their horns when appropriate but should not depend on the horn for safety.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Motorcycles must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: When can motorcycles pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right side of the vehicle. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If chased by a dog, slow down and downshift. As the dog gets close, accelerate quickly and leave it behind.

questions.question: How should a passenger hold on?

options.text: Hold the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. They may also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do in areas with possible dangers?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, shopping centers, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: How should the front brake be used?

options.text: It is not safe to use

questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you easier to see. This works day or night.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.explanation: The gearshift is in front of the left footrest. The rider operates it with their left foot.

questions.question: How many drinks affect a rider's ability?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: If you approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. This is the safest position. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far from it may make the other driver return to your lane too early, which is also dangerous.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to improve your view.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When entering a curve, how should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to see the best and be seen the best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to see the best and be seen the best.
questions.explanation: Adjust your lane position when entering a curve to see better and be more visible. For a left turn, ride on the right side of your lane to see oncoming traffic early. For a right turn, ride on the left center of your lane to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.
